text.p: Salomon Brothers has upgraded its rating for Orbotech Ltd, an Israeli maker of printed circuit board (PCB) inspection equipment, to a strong buy from a buy.

Analyst Victor Halpert said the decline in Orbotech's Nasdaq share price to around $11.50 from $17 in May made the stock very attractive on a price-earnings (PE) basis. Based on Salomon's 1996 forecasted earnings per share (EPS) of $1.49, the company is trading at a PE of 8.4
Based on Salomon's 1997 EPS of $1.73, Orbotech is trading at a PE of 7.2

Halpert attributed the share price drop to market concerns about an expected slowdown in the semiconductors industry, which would have affected the PCB market. However, he said, "recovery of the semiconductors industry should have a direct effect on investors' enthusiasm about Orbotech as the outlook for the industry is brightening".

Halpert pointed to the company's development of new markets in China, South Korea and Japan as well as new product lines for inspecting cathode ray tubes and lead frames for integrated circuits and for processing cheques.
Salomon gave Orbotech an 18-month price target of $22-$25 a share.
